summary: The change canonicalizes per-record reservation ordering before hashing the step fingerprint, so a storage reload that returns reservations in id order no longer re-steps unchanged records. The new fake-port regression proves 60 unchanged records are skipped with no write after a reordered reload, and that a real reservation outcome change still wakes exactly the owning record. No introduced defect found.

evidence: src/repair/step-inputs.ts sorts each task's reservations by id before hashing, so admission append order versus Git reload id order no longer changes the fingerprint.
tests/repair/loop-input-gate_test.ts adds a 60-record fake-port regression: a reordered reservation reload yields recordsSkipped 60, recordsStepped 0 and no state write.
The same test confirms an actual reservation outcome change still steps only the owning record, so the canonicalization does not hide real input changes.
The two-file change leaves src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts and the review, CI, P0 and accounting gates untouched.
